newsitem.title: CHAD: Chad says Cameroon pipeline start delayed.
newsitem.headline: Chad says Cameroon pipeline start delayed.

text.p: Chadian President Idriss Deby said on Friday construction of an oil pipeline to Cameroon had been delayed by several months because the two governments had not yet completed details of the projects.
At a news conference, he complained of interference by French environmentalists who he said were campaigning against development of Chad's oil resources.
Local units of Exxon, Shell and Elf Aquitaine SA are prospecting in the south and west.
Construction of a pipeline to tanker terminals at Cameroon's Kribi port had been due to start at the end of the year.
Deby said the French branch of Friends of the Earth and some Chadians opposed exploiting the oil because the people of the region were not benefiting and because of environmental concerns.

The discovery of significant oil reserves in the southern Doba basin, due to come on stream in 2000, has raised the stakes in the traditional rivalry between the northern and southern parts of landlocked Chad.
"As oil is a national resource, oil revenue will be part of the budget. Oil reserves will be transparently managed for the benefit of the Chadian people," Deby said.
He urged Chadians not to abandon their traditional farming and livestock raising activities in the hope of oil wealth.
"On the contrary, oil revenues should be used for the development of agriculture and livestock raising so that we do not fall into the errors of other African countries with oil reserves," Deby said.
